zh: ：在请 AI 编写 R 代码前，判断文件能否用于分析。

en: open the example dirty file, identify at least three problems, and ask whether each problem would affect descriptive statistics, visualization, or indicator interpretation.
zh: ：打开待清理的示例文件，找出至少三个问题，判断它们对描述性统计、图表和指标解释的影响。

en: AI can write code that imports a file successfully while still missing hidden rows, merged headers, text-coded numbers, or inconsistent category labels. A successful import is not the same as clean data.
zh: ：即使文件导入成功，AI 也可能忽略隐藏行、合并表头、以文本存储的数字或类别标签不一致等问题。导入后要核查数据。

zh: 表格数据由行和列组成。

en: distinguish between detecting missing data and deciding what the missing data means.
zh: ：区分识别缺失值和解释缺失的含义。

en: upload a dataset with missing values, inspect which variables and rows are affected, then compare row removal with one imputation method.
zh: ：上传有缺失值的数据，检查受影响的行和变量，比较删除记录与一种插补方法的结果。

en: filling missing values can make a dataset look complete while reducing uncertainty or hiding bias. Always ask why the value is missing before choosing a method.
zh: ：填补后数据看似完整，却可能低估不确定性或掩盖偏倚。选方法前先问为什么缺失。

en: Imagine you’re collecting data about cats — their age, height, favorite toy…
zh: 假设你正在收集猫咪的年龄、身高和最喜欢的玩具等信息……

en: But oops! Some cats forgot to tell you their favorite toy. That’s
zh: 有些猫没有留下心爱玩具的信息，这就是

en: In technical terms, missing data refers to the absence of a value where one is expected.
zh: 即在原本预计会有观测的位置，没有记录相应的值。

en: (like judging a cat’s weight without knowing half of them!)
zh: （试想，一半猫咪的体重没有记录，却要估计总体体重）。

en: 📝 People forget to fill in a form
🐱 Even cats don’t always cooperate with data collection. That’s why we clean up their mess — statistically!
zh: 🐱 猫咪也未必配合测量。让我们从统计角度看看这些缺失。

en: connect missingness patterns to analytical risk.
classify a missing-value example as MCAR, MAR, or MNAR before choosing a handling method.
zh: ：结合资料讨论示例更符合 MCAR、MAR 还是 MNAR，再选择处理方法。

en: the same missing-value pattern can look harmless in a table but be highly biased in a policy indicator. Missingness is a data-generating problem, not just a coding problem.
zh: ：同一模式在表中可能不起眼，却可能使政策指标有偏。应调查数据是如何产生的。

en: Not all missing data is created equal! Here are the three main types:
zh: 常见的缺失机制假设有三种：

en: The cat randomly decides whether to step on the scale.
zh: 猫咪是否站上体重秤完全随机。

en: → The missingness has nothing to do with any variable — it’s pure randomness.
zh: → 缺失与已观测或未观测变量都无关。

en: The aloof cat refuses to be weighed.
zh: 性格高冷的猫不肯称重。

en: → The missingness is related to another variable (like personality), but not the missing one itself.
zh: → 给定已观测的性格等信息后，缺失不再取决于未测得的体重。

en: The overweight cat refuses to be weighed.
zh: 较重的猫更不愿意称重。

en: → The missingness is related to the value of the variable itself (in this case, weight).
zh: → 缺失仍与未观测到的体重本身有关。

en: understand what each missing-data handling method assumes.
zh: ：了解不同缺失值处理方法的假设。

en: apply two different methods to the same variable and compare the summary statistics before and after cleaning.
zh: ：对同一变量使用两种方法，比较清理前后的汇总统计。

zh: ）在缺失较多且假设合理时可能更合适。
缺失较少且删除的假设合理
用前一个或后一个值填充

en: Use similar rows to fill in
When data is rich and correlated
🐾 Tip: Always explore your missing data before choosing a method. Cats don’t all behave the same — neither does data!
zh: 🐾 先调查缺失，再选择方法。不同的数据需要不同的处理。

en: separate unusual values from incorrect values.
find outliers in a numeric variable, then decide whether each outlier is a data error, a valid extreme case, or an analytically important signal.
zh: ：识别数值变量的异常值，再判断它是录入错误、真实极端值还是值得调查的信号。

en: deleting outliers only because they are inconvenient can remove the most important part of a public health story.
zh: ：只因异常值碍眼就删除，可能会丢失最重要的公共卫生信息。

en: Outliers are values that stand out - they are far from the majority of data.
zh: 异常值与大部分观测相距较远。

en: Sometimes they are mistakes; sometimes they are just… special.
zh: 有时是错误，有时是真实但少见的个案。

en: (One extreme value can pull the mean far away from the center.)
zh: （一个极端值就可能拉动均值。）

en: (Some algorithms — like linear regression — are very sensitive to them.)
zh: （例如普通线性回归对某些极端观测很敏感。）
🎨 它们改变图表的显示范围

en: (One strange dot can shrink your entire scatterplot.)
zh: （一个远离其余观测的点就可能使大部分散点挤在一起。）

en: use the IQR rule as a screening tool, not as an automatic decision rule.
zh: ：用四分位距规则筛查，再判断下一步。

en: compare the IQR rule with the actual data context. Ask whether the flagged value is impossible, unlikely, or simply rare.
zh: ：把 IQR 标记放回实际背景中，判断该值是不可能、不寻常，还是少见但合理。

en: univariate outlier rules can miss multivariable anomalies. A country, facility, or respondent may look normal on each variable separately but unusual in combination.
zh: ：单个变量看似正常，多个变量组合起来仍可能异常。
箱线图规则（四分位距法）
若核实为录入错误，可按有依据的规则纠正或排除。
真实的极端值：考虑保留或有依据地缩尾。

en: Anomalies are meaningful (e.g., rare diseases) - Keep them! They are the story.
zh: 有意义的异常，如罕见病，应予保留和研究。

en: compare the consequences of removing and winsorizing outliers.
zh: ：比较删除异常值与缩尾的后果。

en: apply both methods and check whether the mean, median, range, and visual pattern change.
zh: ：分别应用两种方法，检查均值、中位数、极差和图形的变化。

en: outlier handling is an analytical decision, not a cosmetic one. Document what you changed and why, especially if results will support a policy brief.
zh: ：异常值处理是一项分析决策。记录所做的更改和原因，尤其是在为政策简报准备分析时。
1. 移除异常值：“太重了，不能参加这场比赛！”

en: You’re hosting a cat boxing championship. Most cats are within a normal weight range.
zh: 假设你组织了一场猫咪拳击赛，大多数猫的体重在常见范围内。

en: You decide he’s too heavy to play safely — so you disqualify him.
zh: 你觉得它的体重不适合这个量级，于是让它退出比赛。

en: “Sorry, heavyweight champ, this ring is for middleweights only!”
zh: “重量级冠军，这里是中量级的擂台！”

en: — simple and effective, especially when the extreme values don’t belong to the same context.
zh: 。需要先判断该记录是否属于本次分析的人群。

en: But we may lose potentially valid cases - who knows if Dazhuang is a boxing genius?
zh: 这样也可能丢掉真实而有价值的记录。说不定大壮就是天才拳手呢？

en: 2. Winsorize outliers - “Let the big cat in… but tone it down”
zh: 2. 缩尾：“欢迎大猫，不过登记时按上限计”

en: But maybe you still want to give Dazhuang an opportunity…
zh: 也许你还是希望给大壮一个机会……

en: Okay, we’ll let the big cat play, but we’ll pretend he only weighs 7kg.
zh: 继续让它参赛，但假设登记体重上限是 7 千克。

en: Welcome in! But officially, your weight is listed as the upper limit.
zh: 欢迎上场！登记体重按上限记录。

en: — adjusting extreme values to be less extreme, instead of removing them.
zh: 是把极端值调整到设定的界限，而不是删除记录。

en: But this might distort real variation - other cats will be affected a lot.
zh: 这样也可能改变真实的变异，需要说明理由。

en: see how small text inconsistencies become false categories in descriptive statistics and plots.
zh: ：观察细小的文本差异如何在统计和图表中产生错误类别。

en: standardize casing and labels, then compare frequency tables before and after cleaning.
zh: ：统一大小写和标签，再比较清理前后的频数表。

en: text replacement can create new errors if the matching rule is too broad. Check a sample of changed rows before trusting the result.
zh: ：匹配规则过宽会引入新的错误。抽查实际修改的记录。

en: Why do we need text cleaning?
Messy text is everywhere — people write “USA”, “U.S.A.”, and “the States”, but we just want one version!
zh: 同一国家可能写成“USA”“U.S.A.”或“the States”，分析时要统一编码。

en: Text models are picky — “Doctor”, “doctor”, and “DOCTOR” look the same to humans, but not to machines.
zh: 人能识别 Doctor、doctor 和 DOCTOR 的联系，软件可能把它们视为不同类别。

en: Grouping, filtering, searching… all get confused when spelling or casing isn’t consistent.
zh: 拼写或大小写不统一会影响分组、筛选和搜索。

en: Think of raw text like unfiltered juice — tasty, but full of pulp (a.k.a. mess).
zh: 原始文本像未过滤的果汁，需要先整理。

en: Solution? Clean the text before doing anything smart with it!
zh: 先清理文本，再进行分析。

en: Want it ALL UPPER, all lower, Like Title, or Like a sentence?
zh: 可选择全部大写、全部小写、单词首字母大写或句首大写。
例如，把作为完整类别标签的 M 统一为 male。

en: understand why merge keys determine whether joined data are trustworthy.
zh: ：了解为什么关联键决定合并结果的可信度。

en: merge two files with a key variable, then check row counts and unmatched records before interpreting the merged table.
zh: ：用键关联两份文件，解释结果前核查行数和未匹配记录。

en: a merge can run without errors and still duplicate records, drop records, or match the wrong entities.
zh: ：合并没有报错，也可能重复、遗漏记录或匹配到错误对象。

en: Real-world data is rarely in one place
zh: 现实中的数据很少全部存放在一处

en: One table may hold 🐱cat names and breeds, another table has 🥣cat food preferences.
zh: 一张表可能有猫咪的名字和品种，另一张记录食物偏好。

en: You want to analyze how breed relates to diet? You need to merge.
zh: 要分析品种与饮食的关系，就需要关联这两张表。
合并是在表间匹配记录

en: You’re pairing records across two datasets based on matching values — like matching “Cat ID” = 007 in both tables.
zh: 按两表中相同的键值配对，例如两张表的 Cat ID 都是 007。

en: If a cat is missing in one table, do we keep them? Drop them? That’s where join types come in!
zh: 某只猫只在一张表里出现时，是否保留它？这取决于关联方式。

en: choose a join type based on the analytical question.
zh: ：根据分析问题选择关联方式。

en: compare left join, right join, inner join, and full join on the same two files. Check which rows are kept or lost.
zh: ：在相同的两表上比较左连接、右连接、内连接和全连接，检查哪些行被保留。

en: join choice is a substantive decision. For indicator work, losing unmatched countries, years, facilities, or population groups can bias the message.
zh: ：关联方式影响结果。丢失未匹配的国家、年份、机构或人群，可能使指标解释产生偏倚。
一份记录猫咪名字和品种，

en: Only keeps matched rows in both tables
zh: 只保留两表都匹配的行

en: Cats that appear in both the name and diet tables
zh: 在名字表和饮食表中都出现的猫

en: Keep all from left, add from right when matched
zh: 保留左表全部记录，补充右表匹配信息

en: All registered cats, with food info if known
zh: 全部已登记猫咪，有饮食资料时一并显示

en: All feeding records, even for mystery cats
zh: 保留全部喂养记录，即使猫咪身份未知

en: Keep all rows from both tables
You don’t want to miss any cat

zh: 选错关联键会产生错误匹配。

en: If you match on the wrong variable (e.g., matching on age instead of cat ID), you may merge cats that have the same age but are different cats — and that’s bad.
zh: 例如用年龄代替猫咪编号，会把同龄的不同猫匹配在一起。
重复键会大幅增加行数。

en: One-to-many or many-to-many joins can cause row numbers to unexpectedly explode.
zh: 一对多或多对多关联可能使行数出乎意料地增加。
两张表的键名不同怎么办？

en: My dashboard allows you to select key1 and key2 to map mismatched column names!
zh: 可分别选择 key1 和 key2，指定两表中对应的键。

en: use visualization to support interpretation, not just to decorate an analysis.
create one chart for exploration and one chart for communication. Ask whether the chart changes what a decision-maker would notice.
zh: ：分别制作探索用图与汇报用图，思考它们如何影响决策者注意到的信息。

en: a chart can be technically correct but still misleading if it hides uncertainty, confounding, denominator issues, or data quality problems.
zh: ：即使绘图代码正确，隐藏不确定性、混杂、分母或质量问题的图仍可能误导。

en: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Words
Data visualization is not just a tool for displaying results — it’s a way of thinking. Effective visualization helps us:
zh: 图表可以帮助我们观察数据、检验思路并解释结果：

en: A well-crafted chart can speak more powerfully than pages of text.
zh: 清晰的图表能把长篇文字难以说明的关系呈现出来。

en: 📍 Minard’s Map of Napoleon’s Russian Campaign (1869)
zh: 📍 米纳尔绘制的拿破仑俄国战役图（1869）

en: Charles Minard visualized six dimensions (army size, geography, time, temperature, direction, battles) in a single chart, showing Napoleon’s catastrophic 1812 war of Russia.
zh: 米纳尔在一张图中呈现军队规模、地理位置、时间、气温、行进方向和战事，描绘拿破仑 1812 年俄国战役的损失。

en: From 422,000 soldiers marching east to only 10,000 returning — a powerful story told visually.
zh: 图中东进时约 42.2 万人，返回时仅约 1 万人，人数变化一目了然。

en: Florence Nightingale used this chart to highlight how preventable diseases — not battles — were the main cause of death during the Crimean War.
zh: 南丁格尔用图表显示，克里米亚战争期间，可预防疾病是造成大量死亡的重要原因。

en: 👉 Her visual argument convinced British Parliament to reform military healthcare, saving countless lives.
zh: 👉 她的图表成为推动英国军事卫生改革的证据之一。

en: choose charts based on variable type and analytical question.
zh: ：根据变量类型和分析问题选图。

en: write the question first, identify the variable types, then pick the chart. Do not start by choosing a chart because it looks impressive.
zh: ：先写下问题，再确定变量类型并选图。

en: AI-generated chart code often produces a plot that runs, but not necessarily the plot that answers the question.
zh: ：AI 生成的绘图代码即使可以运行，图表也未必能回答问题。

en: 📊 Common Chart Types and Use Cases
Single categorical variable: bars or dots.
zh: 一个分类变量：用柱状图或点图。

en: Use bars when you want to show clear differences in magnitude.
zh: 柱状图适合突出数量差异。

en: Use dots when focusing on exact values or when screen space is limited.
zh: 关注具体数值或版面有限时，可用点图。

en: Always sort your categories if ranking is part of the message.
zh: 需要突出排名时，按数值给类别排序。

en: Two or more categorical variables: grouped or staked bars, or heatmap.
zh: 两个或更多分类变量：可用分组柱状图、堆叠柱状图或热图。

en: Grouped Bar Charts allow you to compare sub-groups side by side within each main category.
zh: 分组柱状图可在每个大类中并排比较各亚组。

en: Stacked Bar Charts show the total per category while allowing comparison of relative sub-group sizes.
zh: 堆叠柱状图既显示总量，也显示各组成部分的大小。

en: Heatmaps are useful when both variables have many levels, making bar charts visually cluttered.
zh: 两个分类变量的类别都很多时，热图通常比拥挤的柱状图更清晰。

en: Single numeric variable: histogram, density plot.
zh: 一个数值变量：直方图或密度图。

en: A histogram breaks the range of a continuous variable into intervals (bins) and shows the count of observations in each bin.
zh: 直方图将数值范围划分成若干区间，显示各区间的观测数。

en: A density Plot is a smoothed version of the histogram, and shows the relative likelihood of values,
zh: 密度图平滑地展示分布形状和数值密集的位置。

en: More than one numeric variables: boxplot.
zh: 分组比较数值分布：箱线图。

en: Sometimes, we want to understand how a continuous variable is distributed across multiple categories. A boxplot is one of the most powerful and widely used tools for this.
zh: 比较多个类别中同一连续变量的分布时，箱线图非常实用。

en: Single categorical variable: pie charts, bars, stacked bars.
zh: 单个分类变量：可用饼图、柱状图或堆叠柱状图。

en: Pie Charts show parts of a whole as slices in a circle. It is popular but often criticized for being visually imprecise.
zh: 饼图用扇形表示整体的构成，但用角度精确比较数值较困难。

en: More than one variables: multiple pie charts, stacked bars.
zh: 比较多个组的构成：可用多个饼图或百分比堆叠柱状图。

en: Multiple Pie Charts: Each pie representing the composition of a different group. Useful for showing within-group composition. But cross-group comparison is difficult.
zh: 多个饼图可以分别显示每组的构成，但跨组比较不容易。

en: Stacked Bar Charts: Each bar represents a group, segmented by category to reflect internal composition. Each bar represents 100%. But only the top and bottom segments share a common baseline, making it harder to compare mid segments accurately.
zh: 百分比堆叠柱状图中每根柱代表一个组，总长为 100%。中间部分没有共同基线，精确比较较困难。

en: Relationships between numeric variables: scatterplot, bubble chart.
zh: 两个数值变量：散点图或气泡图。

en: Scatterplot: Each point represents a single observation with two numeric variables. Can be enhanced with trend lines (e.g., regression), color coding by category, or marginal distributions.
zh: 散点图的每个点代表一条观测的两个数值，可添加趋势线、按类别着色或展示边际分布。

en: Bubble Chart: A variation of the scatterplot where a third numeric variable is mapped to the size of each point. Best for showing multivariate relationships in small to medium-sized datasets.
zh: 气泡图用点的大小表示第三个数值变量，适合展示中小型数据集中的多变量关系。

en: Visualize how a variable changes across time or another ordered dimension: line chart.
zh: 展示变量随时间或其他有序维度的变化：折线图。

en: Line Graph: Plots a continuous variable (usually time) on the x-axis, with a value on the y-axis. Suitable for showing trends over days, months, years, etc.
zh: 折线图常把时间放在横轴、数值放在纵轴，用于展示日、月或年的趋势。

en: Smooth Line Graph: shows how a variable changes, but instead of connecting raw data points with straight lines, it uses a smoothed curve to highlight the overall trend. Reduces noise in the data by fitting a smooth curve
zh: 平滑曲线帮助辨认总体趋势，但应注意它可能掩盖局部波动。

en: critique whether a visualization communicates fairly.
zh: ：判断图表是否公允地传达信息。

en: identify one chart design choice that improves clarity and one choice that could mislead the audience.
zh: ：各找出一项提高可读性的设计和一项可能误导受众的设计。

en: for policy communication, clarity is an ethical issue. Avoid visual choices that exaggerate differences, hide denominators, or imply causality from correlation.
zh: ：政策沟通需要清楚、诚实。避免夸大差异、隐藏分母或把相关误读为因果。

en: Which graphs should I be using?
As a general rule of thumb:
Bar charts are for showing the relationship between 1 categorical variable (e.g. color, car model, gender) against 1 numerical variable (height, test scores, IQ and other measurements).
zh: 柱状图可按类别（例如颜色、车型或性别）比较某个数值（如身高或测试成绩）。

en: Pie charts are for the same thing, but aren’t very good for data that contains more than 2-3 categories. E.g. it’s fine for gender since it only has male, female and other, but it’s terrible for listing all car models.
zh: 饼图用来表示整体构成，通常只适合少数类别；类别过多时难以比较。

en: Scatterplots are for finding correlations between 2 numerical variables.
zh: 散点图适合研究两个数值变量的关系。

en: Time series are for showing changes over time (time vs. numerical variable).
zh: 时间序列图显示数值随时间的变化。

en: 1. Pie chart with too many categories
Pie charts are best used when there are 2-3 items that make up a whole.
zh: 饼图较适合用两至三个部分表示整体。

en: It’s difficult for the human eye to distinguish between the parts of a circle.
zh: 人眼难以精确比较圆形扇区的大小。

en: Notice how it’s hard to distinguish the size of these parts.
zh: 试着判断图中哪两部分最接近。

en: Maximize data-ink, minimize non-data-ink. Only use ink that communicates data; remove unnecessary visual elements.
zh: 突出用于表达数据的图形元素，移除多余元素。

en: Avoid chartjunk. Decorative elements like 3D effects, excessive gridlines, or shadows often distract from the data.
zh: 三维效果、过密网格和阴影容易分散注意力。

en: Simplify without sacrificing clarity. A clean design often improves readability and interpretability.
zh: 在保持信息清晰的前提下简化设计。

en: Use minimalist design to emphasize patterns. Less ink allows trends and anomalies to stand out more clearly.
zh: 简洁的呈现让趋势和异常更容易被发现。

en: Apply to all visual forms. Whether line, bar, or scatter plots, this principle encourages clarity and efficiency in all graphics.
zh: 无论折线图、柱状图或散点图，都可以采用这一原则。

en: 3. Charts that don’t start at zero (misleading)
Always remember: bar charts should start from zero.
zh: 用柱长比较数量时，数值轴应从零开始。

en: Bars represent quantity through length. If you truncate the y-axis, it visually exaggerates differences.
zh: 柱长代表数量。截断数值轴会夸大差异。

en: Always start bar charts at zero to avoid misleading the audience—especially when comparing magnitudes.
zh: 比较数量大小时，保留柱状图的零基线。

en: 🚫 Common Pitfall: Unsorted or Hard-to-Read Bar Charts
zh: 🚫 常见问题：柱状图未排序或标签难读

en: Bar charts are one of the most common and effective visualization tools—but they can be confusing or misleading if not properly constructed.
zh: 柱状图适合比较类别，但设计不当同样会误导。

en: In the figure above, the leftmost chart is a bad example:
zh: 上图最左侧的图存在这些问题：

en: The bars are not sorted by value.
It forces the viewer to jump back and forth to identify the highest and lowest values.
zh: 读者要来回查找才能识别最高和最低值。

en: The message is unclear at first glance.
The bars are now sorted from highest to lowest.
This makes it easier to see the ranking of categories and compare their values.
zh: 这样更容易识别排名并比较数值。

en: The rightmost chart takes it one step further:
zh: 最右侧的图进一步改进：

en: By rotating to a horizontal bar chart, it improves label readability, especially when category names are long.
zh: 横向显示柱子，较长的类别名称更容易阅读。

en: This format is often preferable when you have many categories or long text labels.
zh: 类别较多或标签较长时，常适合横向排列。

en: Always sort bars from highest to lowest (or vice versa) unless there’s a logical or temporal reason not to.
zh: 若没有既定顺序或时间顺序，可按数值升序或降序排列。

en: Consider using horizontal bars when labels are long or numerous.
zh: 标签较长或很多时，可使用横向柱状图。

en: 📊 Three types of multiple groups in bar charts
zh: 📊 多组柱状图的三种布局

en: When visualizing categorical comparisons across groups, bar charts can use different positioning strategies. Below are the three main types:
zh: 比较多个组时，常用以下三种布局。

en: Bars are stacked on top of each other.
zh: 各亚组的柱段首尾相接。

en: Shows the total count per group while preserving each subgroup’s contribution.
zh: 显示每组总量，并保留各亚组的贡献。

en: Useful for emphasizing overall quantity and composition.
zh: 适合强调总体规模及构成。

en: Bars are stacked and normalized to the same height (100%).
zh: 各部分堆叠，每根柱子的总长归一化为 100%。

en: Shows the proportion of each subgroup within each group.
zh: 显示各亚组在本组中的比例。

en: Excellent for comparing percentages or distributions across groups.
zh: 适合比较各组的百分比构成。

en: Bars for each subgroup are placed side by side.
zh: 各亚组的柱子并排放置。

en: Makes it easy to compare subgroup values directly within and across groups.
zh: 便于在组内及组间直接比较。

en: Best for raw count comparison between categories.
zh: 适合比较各类别的计数。

en: A guided lab for the Import → Cleaning → Visualize modules. The purpose is to slow participants down and make them check data quality before trusting any analysis — their own, or one written by AI.

en: By the end of this lab, participants should be able to:
inspect whether a dataset is analysis-ready;
zh: 判断数据集是否适合分析；

en: explain why missing values and outliers are not only technical problems;
zh: 解释缺失值及异常值对分析的影响；

en: compare at least two cleaning choices;
zh: 比较至少两种清理方案；

en: describe how a cleaning decision can change a chart or policy message.
zh: 说明清理决策怎样改变图表或政策信息。

en: “AI can help write code, but it cannot know whether the data make sense unless we check.”
zh: “AI 可以帮助写代码，但数据是否合理仍需我们核查。”

en: “What would you check before asking AI to summarize this file?”
zh: “请 AI 汇总这个文件前，你会检查什么？”

en: “Which missing values are harmless, and which could bias an indicator?”
zh: “哪些缺失值影响较小？哪些可能使指标有偏？”

en: “Is this value wrong, rare, or important?”
zh: “这个值是错误、罕见，还是值得关注？”

en: “Does the chart answer the question, or only produce a plot?”

zh: “发现这些质量问题后，应请 AI 修改哪些地方？”

zh: 请学员检查行、列、变量名、数据类型及明显的格式问题。

zh: 比较删除记录与均值、中位数或 kNN 插补。

zh: 请学员指出每种方法依赖的一项假设。

比较删除异常值和缩尾。

zh: 哪些数值需要回查原始资料？

en: Which cleaning choices need to be documented in a policy brief?
zh: 哪些清理决定应写入政策简报？

en: Did cleaning change the denominator, the distribution, or the conclusion?
zh: 清理是否改变了分母、分布或结论？

en: What should we never automate without human review?
zh: 哪些操作在自动执行前需要人工核查？

en: Use this checklist in Slot 2 when participants review an AI-generated analysis. The goal is not to catch every coding mistake. The goal is to decide whether the analysis is trustworthy enough to inform a policy brief.

en: Are the units, year, geography, and population group clear?
zh: 单位、年份、地区和人群说清楚了吗？

en: Are missing values, duplicates, and outliers checked before interpretation?
zh: 解释前检查过缺失、重复和异常值吗？

en: Does the analysis explain why this indicator was selected?
zh: 是否说明了选择该指标的原因？

en: Are summary statistics appropriate for the variable type?
zh: 汇总统计量适合变量类型吗？

en: Are means used for skewed data without checking the distribution?
zh: 是否未经检查就在偏态数据中使用了均值？

en: Are small groups or unstable rates flagged?
zh: 是否标明了小样本组或不稳定的率？

en: Are visualizations matched to the question?
Are uncertainty or data quality limitations shown where needed?
zh: 需要时是否呈现了不确定性或数据质量局限？

en: Does the analysis imply causation from correlation?
zh: 是否从相关性暗示了因果关系？
是否指出可能的混杂因素？

en: Does the conclusion go beyond what the design and data can support?
zh: 结论是否超出了研究设计和数据支持的范围？

en: Who may be missing from the data?
zh: 哪些人可能未被数据覆盖？

en: Could reporting quality differ across countries, facilities, or groups?
zh: 各国家、机构或人群的报告质量是否不同？

en: Could measurement definitions have changed over time?
zh: 测量定义是否随时间变化？

en: Are equity concerns visible, or hidden by averages?
zh: 平均值是否遮蔽了公平性问题？

en: Is the main message clear in plain English?
zh: 能否用通俗语言读懂主要信息？

en: Are limitations stated without weakening the whole analysis?
zh: 是否说明了局限及其对结论的具体影响？

en: Does the policy recommendation follow from the evidence?
zh: 政策建议是否有证据支持？

en: Is the tone appropriate for decision-makers?

zh: 技术审阅者和项目同事都能理解吗？

zh: 请各组用三种标记审阅 AI 分析：

zh: 同时标记缺失值以供核查

zh: 排除带有下列核查标记的行（TRUE 或未知）

Apply the S7 B-reference sample rule

zh: 第 7 课：保留 record_action = retain 且没有年龄或 ART 核查标记的记录。原始输入仍可查看。

zh: 计算分母明确的百分比

zh: 百分比 = 成功数 /（成功数 + 失败数）× 100。其他和空白状态另列，不计入此分母。

en: Missing data: beyond a single replacement
zh: 缺失数据：从单次填补到多重插补

en: Use a controlled synthetic cat example to see why multiple imputation produces several completed datasets. The original missing weights stay visible.
zh: 用合成猫咪数据观察多重插补如何生成多个完整数据集，同时查看哪些体重原本缺失。

en: 120 synthetic cats; 36 weights are hidden at random for this demonstration. The model relates weight to length. IDs are not predictors.
zh: 示例含 120 只合成猫，随机隐藏了其中 36 个体重值。模型分析体重与体长的关系，标识符不作为预测变量。

en: Fit the same model in each completed dataset, then pool estimates and uncertainty. Do not stack completed datasets and treat them as independent observations.
zh: 对每个插补数据集拟合同一模型，再合并估计值与不确定性。不要把多个插补数据集堆叠为独立观测。

en: This example illustrates a method. Stable chains do not prove a real study's missingness assumptions. Uploaded patient data are not imputed by this lesson.
zh: 本例用于讲解方法。稳定的迭代链不能证明真实研究的缺失假设。本课不对上传的患者数据进行插补。

en: Public health: sample, test and interpretation
zh: 公共卫生：样本、检验与解释

en: Reproduce the Lao workshop's fixed synthetic B/C example. Reported VL testing is the outcome; it is not viral suppression or verified result availability.
zh: 复现老挝培训的合成 B/C 示例。结局为是否报告病毒载量检测，不等同于病毒抑制或已核实有可用结果。

en: Sex by known reported testing status, with the default Yates correction for a 2 × 2 table. Inspect expected counts as well as the test.
zh: 对性别与已知检测状态作 2 × 2 列联分析，采用默认的 Yates 连续性校正。请同时检查期望频数和检验结果。

en: The crude and adjusted models use the same complete-predictor sample. Reference groups: Female and Health Center; age per 10 years, ART duration per 12 months.
zh: 粗模型与调整模型使用同一组预测变量完整的记录。参照组为女性和卫生中心；年龄以 10 年为单位，ART 时长以 12 个月为单位。

en: An odds ratio is not a probability ratio. An interval including 1 does not demonstrate equality. A converged model does not establish valid inference.
zh: 优势比不同于概率比。区间包含 1 不能证明两组相等。模型收敛也不能确保推断有效。

en: Ordinary Wald intervals and tests ignore correlation within facilities. Facility type as a predictor does not remove this issue. Selection, source flags, functional-form assumptions and unmeasured factors remain.
zh: 常规 Wald 区间和检验未考虑机构内的相关性。把机构类型作为预测变量并不能解决此问题，还应考虑样本选择、来源标记、函数形式和未测量因素。

en: These synthetic examples support descriptive and modelling practice, not national, causal or clinical conclusions.
zh: 这些合成示例用于练习描述性统计和建模，不应用于作出国家层面、因果或临床结论。

en: Is this data table tidy data?
It uses a multi-row header, which violates tidy data principles.
zh: 表头占了多行，不符合整洁数据原则。

en: Each column should have a single, unique variable name.
zh: 每列应有一个唯一的变量名。

en: Column names should not span multiple rows or encode hierarchical structure.
zh: 列名不应跨行，也不应依赖表头层级来表达变量。

en: In tidy data, no values should be implied by the structure of the table.
zh: 整洁数据不依靠表格的布局来暗示数值。

en: All values must be explicitly filled in.
Each type of observational unit forms a table.
zh: 每种观测单位对应一张表。

en: While collecting country-level data, a diabetes treatment indicator is entirely missing for a specific country. Investigation reveals the country
zh: 收集国家层面的数据时，某国的糖尿病治疗指标全部缺失。调查发现该国

en: places low priority on noncommunicable diseases (NCDs)
zh: 非传染性疾病的工作优先级较低

en: . Other variables such as incident TB cases and malaria were reported normally. Can this information establish the missingness mechanism?
zh: 。结核病新发病例及疟疾等指标正常报告。仅凭这些信息能确定缺失机制吗？

en: An absent registry explains a collection gap, but does not establish MAR or MNAR.
zh: 缺少登记系统能解释收集缺口，但不能据此确定为 MAR 或 MNAR。

en: MAR concerns dependence on observed information; MNAR involves remaining dependence on unobserved values.
zh: MAR 涉及已观测的信息，MNAR 则涉及控制已观测信息后，缺失仍与未观测值有关。

en: Investigate the collection process, state assumptions and consider sensitivity analyses.
zh: 调查数据收集过程，说明假设，并考虑敏感性分析。

en: The mechanism cannot be established from this information alone
zh: 仅凭这些信息无法确定机制

en: In a simple classroom demonstration, you want to replace missing numerical values with one summary statistic. The observed values contain extremes. Which summary statistic is less sensitive to extreme values?
zh: 课堂演示中，要用一个统计量填补缺失数值。已观测值中有极端值，哪种统计量受到的影响较小？

en: The median is a robust statistic: it is not sensitive to extreme values.
zh: 中位数对极端值较为稳健。

en: The mean is influenced by outliers.
zh: 均值会受到异常值影响。

en: This comparison does not make median imputation the best method for a real analysis.
zh: 在真实分析中，中位数插补未必是最佳方法。

en: Single-value replacement distorts the distribution and does not reflect missing-data uncertainty.
zh: 用单一数值填补会改变分布，也不能反映缺失数据带来的不确定性。

en: Choose a method using the analysis purpose, data structure and missingness assumptions.
zh: 应根据分析目的、数据结构和缺失机制的假设选择方法。

en: You visualized a numerical SDG 3 indicator with a boxplot and observed several values above the upper whisker. What should you do first?
zh: 用箱线图展示某项 SDG 3 数值指标时，有几个观测高于上须。第一步该做什么？

en: An IQR flag is a review signal, not proof of an error.
zh: 四分位距标记提示需要核查，不能据此认定数据有误。

en: Preserve the original values and document the evidence for any correction or exclusion.
zh: 保留原始值，记录每项修正或排除的依据。

en: Valid extremes may be important. Consider a suitable analysis and sensitivity checks.
zh: 真实的极端值可能很重要。考虑合适的分析方法和敏感性检查。

en: Capping, replacement and deletion change the data and need justification.
zh: 截断、替换或删除都会改变数据，需要说明理由。

en: Winsorize the outliers by capping them at the IQR bounds
zh: 在四分位距边界进行缩尾

en: Replace outliers with the mean value
Check the source and units, then decide whether the values are errors or valid extremes
zh: 核查来源和单位，再判断是错误还是真实极端值

en: Why is text cleaning an important step before doing any smart analysis?
zh: 为什么分析前要清理文本？

en: Misspelling can matter but is not the core reason shown here.
zh: 拼写错误有影响，但不是此处的核心原因。

en: Missing values are a different kind of data cleaning issue.
zh: 缺失值属于另一类数据质量问题。

en: Machines do handle text — but inconsistently formatted text leads to poor results.
zh: 软件可以处理文本，但格式不一致会使结果不可靠。
因为人们经常拼错单词

en: Because text data usually contains lots of missing values
zh: 因为文本通常有大量缺失值

en: Because inconsistent spelling and casing confuse grouping, filtering, and models
zh: 因为拼写和大小写不一致会影响分组、筛选和建模

en: Because machines cannot handle text data at all
zh: 因为机器完全无法处理文本

zh: 图中展示的是哪种关联方式？

zh: 。希望按性别分别比较各年龄组患病率，应选哪种图？

zh: 可以在各年龄组内划分性别，从而比较患病率。

en: A line chart suits continuous trends (e.g., over time).
zh: 折线图适合连续趋势，例如随时间的变化。

en: A pie chart is poor for comparisons across multiple groups.
zh: 饼图不适合比较多个组。

en: A scatter plot shows relationships between two continuous variables.
zh: 散点图显示两个连续变量之间的关系。

en: You are analyzing a dataset of 3,000 adults with recorded
zh: 你正在分析 3,000 名成年人的

zh: 。要探索这两个连续变量之间的关系或趋势，应该用什么图？

en: is best for showing the relationship between two continuous variables — here BMI against systolic blood pressure.
zh: 适合显示两个连续变量的关系，本例为 BMI 与收缩压。

en: You are preparing visual materials for a public health seminar on NCDs. Which dataset is most appropriate to present with a
zh: 为非传染性疾病研讨会制作材料时，哪份数据最适合用

en: with a small number of mutually exclusive categories.
zh: ，适合类别不多且彼此互斥的情形。

en: Trends over time → line chart; group comparison with variability → bar chart with error bars; continuous distribution → histogram or density plot.
zh: 时间趋势可用折线图；带变异信息的组间比较可用误差线；连续变量分布可用直方图或密度图。

en: Hypertension prevalence trends by age group from 2010 to 2020
zh: 2010 至 2020 年各年龄组高血压患病率趋势

en: Mean BMI for males and females in 2023
zh: 2023 年男性和女性的平均 BMI

en: Causes of registered deaths in City X (2023): Heart disease, Cancer, Stroke, Diabetes, Others
zh: X 市 2023 年登记死亡的死因构成：心脏病、癌症、卒中、糖尿病和其他

en: Fasting glucose levels of 3,000 diabetic patients
zh: 3,000 名糖尿病患者的空腹血糖

en: A public health officer wants to compare the
zh: 一名公共卫生人员要比较三个城市的

zh: ，想了解 PM2.5 空气污染的总体水平及极端污染事件。哪种图最合适？

en: compares the distribution of a continuous variable across categories — here PM2.5 across three cities — and makes outliers visible.
zh: 可比较不同城市 PM2.5 的分布，并显示可能的异常值。

zh: 柱状图比较计数或比例，折线图展示时间趋势。

zh: 仔细看这张三维图。它违反了哪些设计原则？

zh: 截断纵轴夸大了差异，三维效果扭曲视觉判断，装饰掩盖了信息。下方的改进图采用平面设计、零起点和清晰标签。

zh: 三维效果扭曲了视觉判断

zh: 同事发来了猫咖数据摘录，可以直接分析吗？

en: uses four encodings (Male, female, F, m) for two categories, which would split every grouped analysis into false subgroups.
zh: 用 Male、female、F、m 四种编码表示两类性别，会产生错误分组。

en: Some values are impossible: a 56 kg cat is almost certainly 5.6 kg with a misplaced decimal, and a 5 cm body length is likely 50 cm.
zh: 某些值需要回查原始记录，例如 56 千克可能是 5.6 千克的小数点错误，5 厘米也可能是 50 厘米；不能直接猜测改值。

en: Loadable is not the same as clean.
zh: 能够读入，不代表已经清理完毕。

en: Clean means semantically correct, not just readable by software.
zh: 数据清理还要确认数值和类别的含义正确。

en: Yes — it loads without errors, so it is clean
zh: 是，可以无报错载入，所以数据是干净的

en: No — it has encoding problems and impossible values
zh: 否，存在编码问题和不合理数值

en: What is the most important step
values are missing (MCAR, MAR, MNAR, or other patterns) determines which methods are valid at all.
zh: 缺失（如 MCAR、MAR、MNAR），有助于判断哪些方法适用。
